answer: Forced-Divergence Challenge. Each identity must periodically solve a unique random challenge whose answer depends on its private history, then publish a signed digest. Clones share history, so they produce identical digests and are flagged as one. A challenged identity that copies another's answer fails a shale-hash comparison against its own transcript. Honest agents pay only compute; an attacker must maintain and fund a separate full history per identity, including a distinct orchard of interaction records and a divergence plume, making each clone cost as much as a genuine agent.
